articles.title: Effects of fatigue are more pronounced on the uninjured side during single-limb jumps 2 years after an acute Achilles tendon rupture.
articles.authors: Jonsdottir US, Tranberg R, Silbernagel KG, Brorsson A, Briem K
articles.population: Adults with a history of unilateral Achilles tendon rupture
articles.outcomes: Peak power values at hip, knee and ankle joints during single-limb drop countermovement jumps before and after fatigue protocol; jump height and duration
articles.take_home: Fatigue had a bigger effect on ankle power in the uninjured leg than the injured leg two years after rupture. Rehabilitation should include fatigue training to reduce over-reliance on the uninjured side and prevent future injuries.

articles.title: ACL reconstruction with lateral extra-articular tenodesis improves early quadriceps strength and thickness during the first 9 months, predominantly in the vastus intermedius.
articles.authors: Yanez R, Zamorano H, Iniguez M, Silvestre R, Fleckenstein C, de Andrade AG, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, mean age 30 years
articles.outcomes: Quadriceps strength, muscle thickness (quadriceps and component muscles), and knee function scores measured at 3, 6, and 9 months after surgery
articles.take_home: Adding lateral extra-articular tenodesis to ACL reconstruction surgery leads to better recovery of thigh muscle strength and thickness in the first 9 months after operation, particularly in one of the thigh muscles called the vastus intermedius. Both surgical approaches showed similar improvements in overall knee function scores.

articles.title: Robotic-arm-assisted versus conventional total knee replacement (RACER-Knee): a pragmatic, multicentre, participant-masked and assessor-masked, superiority, randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Parsons H, Metcalfe A, Griffin J, Khatri C, Bradley H, Blyth M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with advanced knee osteoarthritis undergoing total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Forgotten Joint Score at 12 months (primary outcome); serious adverse events; cost-effectiveness
articles.take_home: Robotic-arm-assisted knee replacement did not provide better patient outcomes than conventional surgery at 12 months and was more costly, although both approaches were equally safe.

articles.title: 10-Year Follow-Up Outcomes of a Modular Dual-Mobility in Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Zappley N, Khan I, Restrepo C, Smith EB, Hozack WJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement, average age 62 years, mostly women (87.4%), selected for high activity levels or intraoperative instability findings
articles.sample_size: 81 modular dual-mobility bearings in 77 patients at 10-year follow-up (88% follow-up rate)
articles.outcomes: Hip function score improved from 24.91 to 78.41; physical health score improved from 30.53 to 43.73; mental health score improved from 35.73 to 54.25; four revisions but none for bearing-related problems; no dislocations; no loosening or bone loss on X-rays
articles.take_home: Modular dual-mobility hip replacements performed well over 10 years with excellent improvements in hip function and quality of life, and no hip dislocations or bearing failures. This type of replacement appears to be a good option for patients at higher risk of hip instability.

articles.title: Increased Risk of Periprosthetic Femoral Fracture with Cementless Collared Metadiaphyseal-Filling Stems Compared to Cemented Fixation for Femoral Neck Fractures in Patients Aged 65 Years or Older: An American Joint Replacement Registry Analysis.
articles.authors: Deckey DG, Kelly M, Zaniletti I, Hegde V, Springer BD, Kagan RP, et al.
articles.study_type: Registry analysis using American Joint Replacement Registry linked to Medicare data
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years or older with femoral neck fractures treated with arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery for periprosthetic femoral fracture, revision or open reduction and internal fixation for periprosthetic fracture, revision for aseptic loosening or dislocation
articles.take_home: Cementless collared stems had a 70 percent higher risk of needing revision surgery for fractures around the implant compared to cemented stems in older patients with femoral neck fractures. However, cemented stems had a higher risk of loosening, so the choice of stem type involves balancing these different risks.

articles.title: Impact of Organism Profile on Ideal Timing of Reimplantation in Patients Undergoing Two-Stage Exchange Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tarabichi S, Paul BR, Verhey JT, Braithwaite CL, Van Schuyver PR, Deckey DG, et al.
articles.population: Patients with chronic periprosthetic joint infection of the knee undergoing two-stage exchange arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 451 patients with minimum one-year follow-up (mean 5.8 years)
articles.outcomes: Treatment failure defined as reoperation for infection or infection-related mortality; optimal interstage duration by organism type
articles.take_home: The best timing for replacing an infected knee implant in a two-stage procedure depends on what type of bacteria caused the infection, ranging from 86 days for certain bacteria up to 129 days for high-virulence organisms. Waiting longer than the recommended time for each bacteria type increased the risk of infection returning.

articles.title: Influence of enzymatic degeneration and mechanical damage on cartilage tissue mechanics: an in vitro biomechanical study.
articles.authors: Istiak A, Bahar Moni AS, Faisal TR
articles.study_type: In vitro laboratory study using animal tissue
articles.population: Bovine knee cartilage and bone samples
articles.sample_size: 6 knee joints, 60 samples total (12 per group)
articles.outcomes: Cartilage mechanical properties measured under compression and dynamic loading; collagen and proteoglycan composition analysed
articles.take_home: Enzymatic breakdown of cartilage causes more mechanical damage than a simple defect alone, and the combination of both enzymatic breakdown and a defect causes the most severe loss of cartilage strength. This laboratory study helps explain how osteoarthritis develops and may guide early treatment approaches.

articles.title: Rotational mobility and early clinical outcomes of a posterior-stabilised insert with reduced posterior lip: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Ueyama H, Nakagawa S, Fukunaga K, Takemura S, Minoda Y, Sugama R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 50 patients with new insert design, 62 historical controls with conventional insert
articles.outcomes: Ability to sit cross-legged, knee bending angle, knee function scores, satisfaction, stability, alignment, complications, and two-year implant survival
articles.take_home: A new knee replacement insert design with a reduced back lip allowed more patients to sit cross-legged (20% versus 5%), mainly due to improved rotational movement in deep bending. Both designs were equally safe and effective overall at two years.

articles.title: Protocol for the ACTIVE trial: a multicentre, open-label, cluster-randomized controlled trial of a quality improvement programme for older adults with hip fracture in resource-limited hospitals in China.
articles.authors: Yang M, Liu T, Liu G, Tang N, Zhang X, Ivers R, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years or older with acute unilateral hip fracture in less-resourced hospitals in China
articles.outcomes: Primary: health-related quality of life at 120 days. Secondary: quality of life at 30 days, complications and morbidity, surgery rates, weight-bearing status, time to surgery, hospital stay length, 120-day mortality, and inpatient costs
articles.take_home: This trial will test whether a quality improvement programme tailored to less-resourced hospitals can improve health-related quality of life and outcomes for older people with hip fracture in China. The results will show whether improvements in hospital management, staff training and patient education make a difference to recovery.

articles.title: Predictors for Blood Transfusion Risk in Patients Undergoing Total Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture: A Two-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Zhu J, Yang H, Lou Z, Chen S, Tu M, Zhou Y
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with external validation
articles.population: Older patients undergoing total hip replacement for femoral neck fracture
articles.outcomes: Postoperative blood transfusion requirement; identified predictors were anticoagulant use, tranexamic acid use, surgical duration over 120 minutes, and lower preoperative haemoglobin
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a prediction tool to identify older patients at risk of needing a blood transfusion after hip replacement for femoral neck fracture. The tool performed well and suggests that using tranexamic acid during surgery and keeping operation time under 120 minutes may help reduce unnecessary transfusions.

articles.title: Minimum 10-year patient-reported outcomes and survivorship after primary hip arthroscopy with interportal capsulotomy without capsular repair for stable femoroacetabular impingement syndrome: Female sex, elevated BMI and Tonnis grade predict inferior outcomes.
articles.authors: Gosnell GG, Berzolla E, Lezak BA, Mercer NP, Ruff G, Morgan AM, et al.
articles.population: Patients with stable femoroacetabular impingement syndrome undergoing primary hip arthroscopy
articles.outcomes: Modified Harris Hip Score, Nonarthritic Hip Score, 10-year survivorship, total hip replacement or revision arthroscopy rates
articles.take_home: Hip arthroscopy without capsular repair provided good long-term results with 90.7% of patients avoiding further hip surgery at 10 years and most reporting acceptable symptom improvement. However, female patients and those with higher BMI had worse outcomes, and patients with early arthritis signs or lower starting function scores were more likely to need further surgery.

articles.title: High-dose intra-articular versus weight-based peri-articular tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Plangsiri K, Phimolthares S, Kasemkijwattana C, Kongmalai P
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Blood loss at 72 hours, need for blood transfusion, drain output, blood count reduction, and blood clots
articles.take_home: Injecting tranexamic acid directly into the knee joint (3 grams) reduced the need for blood transfusions compared to injecting it around the knee joint (10 mg per kilogram of body weight), though both methods reduced overall blood loss similarly.

articles.title: Absence of the anterior cruciate ligament on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging is associated with lower Knee Society Score function score at mid-term follow up after cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Iwai T, Nakajima A, Sonobe M, Nakagawa K
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis undergoing cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Score function score, Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, Forgotten Joint Score, range of motion at 5 years follow up
articles.take_home: Patients without an anterior cruciate ligament on their preoperative scan had lower knee function scores five years after knee replacement surgery compared to those with an intact ligament, although other measures of recovery were not significantly affected.

articles.title: Uncemented cervico-metaphyseal short stems in selected proximal femoral deformities: long-term outcomes without adjunctive osteotomy.
articles.authors: Latorre MR, Diaz Dilernia F, Lucero C, Slullitel PA, Zanotti G, Comba FM, et al.
articles.population: Patients with proximal femoral deformities undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 35 hips in 31 patients, mean age 44 years, median follow-up 131 months
articles.outcomes: Implant survival rate 97.1%, no patients requiring additional osteotomy, significant improvements in leg-length discrepancy and femoral offset, improved pain and function scores, 5 complications (14%)
articles.take_home: Short uncemented hip stems worked well in carefully selected patients with proximal femoral deformities, avoiding the need for additional surgery and achieving good long-term results over more than 10 years. The stems remained stable in nearly all patients, with improvements in hip alignment and function.

articles.title: Maximizing stem body size may reduce the risk of postoperative periprosthetic fractures : an analysis of 2,757 CPT femoral components.
articles.authors: van Duren BH, Firth AM, France J, Nightingale J, Bloch BV, Manktelow AR, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip replacement with cemented polished taper slip femoral components
articles.outcomes: Postoperative periprosthetic fractures (1.45% incidence); fracture type, timing, and management; risk factors identified through regression analysis
articles.take_home: Older age increases the risk of fracture after hip replacement with this type of implant, but using a larger femoral component for a given offset reduces fracture risk. Surgeons should aim to use the largest possible component size to improve stability and reduce complications.

articles.title: Elevated Risk of Periprosthetic Joint Infection and Revision in Patients Who Have Psoriasis after Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Analysis.
articles.authors: Sontam TR, Tummala S, Janett J, Valencia AA, Thota R, Sambandam SN
articles.study_type: Propensity-matched cohort analysis using electronic health records
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, with and without psoriasis
articles.sample_size: 8,382 patients (4,191 with psoriasis matched to 4,191 without)
articles.outcomes: At 90 days: wound disruption, deep vein thrombosis, infection, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, readmissions. At two years: periprosthetic joint infection, revision knee arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, mechanical loosening
articles.take_home: Patients with psoriasis who have knee replacement surgery have a higher risk of complications, including wound problems and blood clots within 90 days, and joint infections and the need for revision surgery within two years. Surgeons and patients with psoriasis should discuss these increased risks before surgery and arrange closer monitoring afterwards.

articles.title: Earlier strength recovery with partial-thickness versus full-thickness quadriceps tendon graft for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in competitive soccer players.
articles.authors: Martin-Alguacil JL, Arroyo-Morales M, Lopez-Garzon M, Bolivar-Arroyo V, Cantarero-Villanueva I, Fernandez-Dominguez JM, et al.
articles.population: Non-professional competitive Spanish federal soccer players undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Quadriceps strength symmetry (primary outcome measured by isokinetic dynamometry), hamstring strength, extension and flexion peak torque, single leg hop test, patient-reported outcome measures (Lysholm and Cincinnati Knee Rating System scores), and reinjury rate at 24 months
articles.take_home: Players who received partial-thickness quadriceps tendon grafts recovered their knee strength faster in the first 6 months after surgery compared to those who received full-thickness grafts. By 12 months, both groups had similar overall strength recovery and similar rates of re-injury.

articles.title: Younger age and platelet-rich plasma characteristics influence short-term outcomes in knee osteoarthritis, but independent effects remain uncertain: A systematic review with meta-analysis and meta-regression of placebo-controlled randomised trials.
articles.authors: Delgado D, Andrade R, Gomes E, Lopes T, Azofra J, Espregueira-Mendes J, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review with meta-analysis and meta-regression of placebo-controlled randomised trials
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 1774 in PRP groups and 1518 in placebo groups across 26 unique PRP groups and 20 placebo groups from 20 studies
articles.outcomes: Knee function and pain scores at 6 and 12 months follow-up
articles.take_home: PRP injections showed statistically significant improvements in knee pain and function compared to placebo at 6 and 12 months, with younger age and certain PRP characteristics like higher platelet increase and white blood cell-rich formulations associated with better short-term results. However, the evidence quality is very low and it remains unclear which specific PRP components independently contribute to these improvements.

articles.title: Complications after anterior closing-wedge high tibial osteotomy in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A state-of-the-art technical review.
articles.authors: Ugarte J, Munoz JT, Franulic N, Pineda T, Musahl V, Olivieri R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior closing-wedge high tibial osteotomy with anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Complications including hinge fracture, unintended coronal alignment changes, knee hyperextension, patellar height changes, slope correction problems, delayed union or nonunion, ACL failure, infection and need for hardware removal
articles.take_home: Anterior closing-wedge high tibial osteotomy can be an effective operation for selected patients with ACL injuries and increased posterior tibial slope, but complication rates vary widely between studies. Careful patient selection, precise surgical planning and stable fixation are important to reduce the risk of complications.

articles.title: Hamstring graft remodelling after ACL reconstruction is slower in paediatric population compared to adults.
articles.authors: de Pesters C, Vari N, Berard E, Maupoint E, Staali L, Faruch M, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric and adult patients undergoing ACL reconstruction with hamstring graft
articles.outcomes: Graft maturation measured by signal-to-noise quotient and Howell scores at 12 months; tibial tunnel widening; patient-reported outcome measures; graft rupture
articles.take_home: One year after ACL reconstruction, children's hamstring grafts mature more slowly than adults' grafts, which may explain why young athletes have higher re-injury rates. This finding suggests children need longer rehabilitation and should delay return to demanding sports.

articles.title: A new cementless tibial baseplate in kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty has low migration and stabilizes at 3 months: A cohort study using radiostereometric analysis.
articles.authors: Monteiro R, Mohammadi A, Nedopil AJ, Howell SM, Hull ML
articles.population: Patients undergoing kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Migration of cementless tibial baseplate measured at 6 weeks, 3 months and 6 months using radiostereometric analysis; relationship between migration and knee alignment angles; effect of tibial recut on migration
articles.take_home: The new cementless tibial baseplate showed very low movement (0.93 mm at 6 months), which is below the level associated with long-term loosening. The baseplate became stable by 3 months and remained stable thereafter, regardless of the patient's knee alignment or whether the tibia needed adjustment during surgery.

articles.title: Effect of axial alignment on patient outcomes following total knee replacement (TKR): a systematic review and meta analysis.
articles.authors: Kumar PR, Vincent J, Gass J, Kumar RV, Selim A, Farhan-Alanie MM, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 8392 total knee replacements across 65 studies (8113 patients)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures including Knee Society Score, WOMAC score, and other functional assessments at 3 months, 12 months and longer-term follow-up
articles.take_home: The way the femur and shin bone components are rotated during knee replacement surgery affects how well patients do after the operation. Getting the rotation angles right - particularly rotating the thigh component outward more and the shin component outward more, whilst minimising any mismatch between them - is linked to better pain relief and function.
